criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a new drain test with max_in_flight = 2 and read_ahead = 1, driven through drain_concurrent, shows the next item's read (and plan, if the job is hard) is requested while the current job is still running, and never more than read_ahead items ahead.
criteria.evidence: 14 tests passed (ran it). `read_ahead_reads_and_plans_the_next_hard_job_while_the_current_one_runs` calls `drain_concurrent(world, limits, &Quiet, 2)` with read_ahead 1. It asserts start a < end a, read b < plan_ahead b < plan b < end a, and end a < read c < end b. It asserts `widest` (reads made minus runs ended) <= 2, that each item is read once, and that spend covers b's plan only. `read_ahead_never_runs_further_ahead_than_the_window` (read_ahead 2) asserts b and c are read before end a and d after it, with widest <= 3. Further tests cover the shared-CHANGELOG case, path clashes, the budget fit and stop handling.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test: a test shows that when the running job changes paths the read-ahead reading touches, that reading is marked stale and the touched paths are re-checked when the job starts; a reading whose paths are untouched is used as is.
criteria.evidence: 5 tests passed (ran it). `stale_reading_is_rechecked_when_its_job_starts`: a lands src/b.rs. The log order is read b < land a < recheck b [src/b.rs] < reread b < start b-fresh. There is one stale note naming b and src/b.rs, and the stale reading is never run. `stale_reading_not_marked_when_paths_are_untouched` and `..._only_shared_files_landed`: no recheck, no reread, no stale note, b is read once and runs on that reading. The production code doing this is `Drain::vet` and `stale_paths` in drain.rs.

findings.summary: Read-ahead is off in production: RealSteps keeps the defaults read_ahead 0, no plan_ahead and recheck true, and does not read `Config.drain.pipeline.read_ahead`. The accepted reading said read_ahead would be read from that config.
findings.evidence: Grep finds no use of `.pipeline` or `read_ahead` outside config.rs and drain.rs. main.rs passes `[parallel] max_concurrency` to drain_concurrent. Leaving it off is the safe choice: wiring read_ahead from config would turn read-ahead on whenever max_concurrency > 1, even with max_in_flight = 1. The planned demonstrations also said the real steps would not turn it on. Still, the engine has no production user, and the reading's assumption is not met.
findings.location: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs:465-495 (Steps defaults); RealSteps impl around line 2217

findings.summary: Changelog and doc comments say the pipeline settings are wired in at build job 10, but the design's job 10 is only the athena.toml change to max_in_flight = 3. No listed build job wires RealSteps' read_ahead, plan_ahead, recheck and reread.
findings.evidence: The changelog says "nothing reads ahead in production until the pipeline settings are wired in (build job 10)". Design job 10 reads: "Set `max_in_flight = 3` in `athena.toml` ... watch the per-landed-job minutes". A follow-up job, or a design note, should name where that wiring happens.

findings.summary: The default `Steps::recheck` returns true, so steps that do not override it run a reading found stale as is. Design section 4 says the drain queues a fresh reading when the paths overlap.
findings.evidence: Design section 4: "re-checks the touched paths when the job starts, and queues a fresh reading if they overlap". vet() rereads only when recheck returns false. Real steps keep read-ahead off today, so there is no production effect yet. A safer default would be recheck false, so an overlap leads to a reread, as the design says.

findings.summary: pick_ahead checks that one read plus one run fits the budget for each new read-ahead, but does not keep the run cap for readings already held ahead. With read_ahead above 1, readings can be paid for that the budget then cannot run.
findings.evidence: `!st.budget.fits(self.caps.read + self.caps.run)` counts only budget holds and spend. The run caps of entries already in `st.ahead` are not held. Any such waste is reported in the notes as "made ahead but not used".

summary: I read the full diff of drain.rs, read sections 4, 11 and 12 of docs/design/async-drain.md, and ran the targeted tests. The change adds read-ahead to `drain_concurrent`. A pump thread reads items, and plans hard ones through `Steps::plan_ahead`, up to `read_ahead` items ahead of the running batch. It skips items whose paths clash with a job still in flight, using a copy of the plan's disjoint-paths rule that a test checks against `Plan::build`. Read-ahead calls are held against the budget and the job limit. At job start the drain compares the paths landed since the reading began with the reading's touched paths. On a hit it writes a stale note and asks `Steps::recheck`, and calls `Steps::reread` if the reading no longer holds. With a bound of 1, or `read_ahead` 0, the pump never starts. My runs: 14 read_ahead tests, 5 stale_reading tests and all 100 tests in tests/drain.rs pass. `git log -L` shows the existing `mod tests` bodies are unchanged. Only drain.rs and CHANGELOG.md changed. The recorded fmt, clippy and test checks pass. Every criterion is met. Three minor findings. The real steps keep the defaults, so read-ahead is off in production. The reading said read_ahead would come from `Config.drain.pipeline`, and it does not yet. The default `recheck` keeps a stale reading, while the design says to queue a fresh one. The changelog says the settings get wired in at build job 10, but the design's job 10 only edits athena.toml.
